question: What is the primary clinical consequence of prolonged malnutrition in hospitalized patients?
explanation: Malnutrition starves the body of essential building blocks and energy required for tissue repair and cellular regeneration, directly prolonging recovery times. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T007#GNS227_U1_T007_h1)

question: Why is dietary assessment considered as fundamental as monitoring vital signs in nursing care?

options.A: Dietary logs are legally required on every shift chart in Nigerian hospitals
options.B: Metabolic rates remain constant regardless of the patient's underlying illness
options.C: Nutrient intake directly dictates the body's capacity to heal and maintain immune competence
options.D: Food consumption is the only reliable indicator of gastrointestinal motility

explanation: Just like vitals show current physiological status, nutritional intake reveals whether the body has the raw materials needed to sustain life and fight disease. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T007#GNS227_U1_T007_h1)

question: What is a major nutritional advantage of animal-based food sources over many plant sources?

options.A: They provide the exclusive source of water-soluble B-complex vitamins
options.B: They supply high biological value proteins containing all essential amino acids
options.C: They contain zero saturated fats and high amounts of soluble dietary fibre
options.D: They are completely free from microbial contamination prior to cooking

explanation: Animal proteins are termed complete because they provide every single amino acid the human body cannot synthesize on its own. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T007#GNS227_U1_T007_h2)

question: Why do traditional Nigerian meal combinations often pair grains or legumes with crayfish or fish?

options.A: To increase the overall glycemic index of the carbohydrate portion
options.B: To complement amino acid profiles and achieve a complete protein intake
options.C: To neutralize natural toxins present in unrefined plant oils
options.D: To eliminate all traces of antinutrients found in raw root vegetables

explanation: Plant foods often lack one or more essential amino acids, so pairing them with animal sources like crayfish ensures the body receives all necessary building blocks. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T007#GNS227_U1_T007_h2)

question: Which category of functional foods do fruits and vegetables primarily belong to?
explanation: Fruits and vegetables are rich in micronutrients and antioxidants that regulate body processes and shield the immune system from disease. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T007#GNS227_U1_T007_h3)

question: A patient recovering from extensive surgical debridement requires a diet rich in which functional food group?
explanation: Surgical recovery requires tissue repair and synthesis, making protein-dense body-building foods the primary nutritional priority. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T007#GNS227_U1_T007_h3)

question: Which chemical category includes vitamins and minerals?
explanation: Vitamins and minerals are classified as micronutrients because the body requires them in very small quantities daily. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T007#GNS227_U1_T007_h4)

question: What is the primary difference in how the body utilizes macronutrients compared to micronutrients?

options.A: Micronutrients supply the bulk of cellular energy, while macronutrients act solely as catalysts
options.B: Macronutrients provide bulk structure and energy, whereas micronutrients regulate metabolic pathways
options.C: Macronutrients are stored indefinitely in bone tissue, while micronutrients are instantly excreted
options.D: Micronutrients can be synthesized in large amounts by the liver, unlike macronutrients

explanation: Macronutrients form the physical mass and caloric fuel of the diet, while micronutrients act as essential cofactors in biochemical reactions. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T007#GNS227_U1_T007_h4)

question: Which food item is classified as perishable?
explanation: Fresh vegetables have high moisture content and spoil quickly, making them highly perishable compared to dried grains or sealed cans. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T007#GNS227_U1_T007_h5)

question: Why are non-perishable foods less susceptible to rapid microbial spoilage?

options.A: They contain high concentrations of artificial chemical preservatives
options.B: They possess low moisture content which inhibits bacterial and fungal growth
options.C: They are completely sterile when harvested from the farm
options.D: They lack the carbon molecules required for microorganism metabolism

explanation: Microorganisms require water to grow and multiply; foods with low moisture content deprive pathogens of this essential environment. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T007#GNS227_U1_T007_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of conducting a nutritional screening upon hospital admission?

options.A: To calculate the exact financial cost of hospital catering
options.B: To determine the patient's religious affiliation and fasting days
options.C: To identify existing or potential nutritional deficits early
options.D: To diagnose underlying genetic metabolic disorders instantly

explanation: Early screening catches malnutrition risks before they manifest as severe clinical complications, guiding timely dietary interventions. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T007#GNS227_U1_T007_h6)

question: A toddler admitted to a pediatric ward presents with bilateral pitting edema, apathy, and dry, brittle hair. Deficiencies in which food classification are primarily responsible for these clinical signs?
explanation: The clinical presentation describes kwashiorkor, a form of severe protein malnutrition caused by a lack of protein-rich body-building foods. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T007#GNS227_U1_T007_h6)
